title: Nick Saban: "I agree with everything that Pat's saying, and that's the underbelly of college athletics, which is really in a bad place right now. But in spite of all that, doing Gameday every week -- we go to all these campuses -- the tradition, the spirit, the enthusiasm, the fan support -- I think a lot of what we see now in college athletics right now and the popularity of it continues to grow, and I think a lot of it was expanding the playoffs to 12 teams camouflaged a lot of these issues and problems over the last few years. "A lot of people are, like, excited about what's happening even though they disagree with the way it's happening -- for all the reasons that you just stated. I think the combination of those two things does not create the sense of urgency that we need to get something done to change it, because they see the popularity, they see the enthusiasm, they see the passion. But the consequence of what we're doing right now is gonna be disastrous if we don't get it fixed."

title: NFL agent Pat Dye Jr. at the Nick Saban Legacy Awards tonight in Birmingham: "It's unbelievable when you think about -- 10 years ago, 8 years ago, whatever before NIL hit, if the NCAA had said to the Power 5 programs, we'll pay each of your scholarship football players $5,000 a month, the players would have done cartwheels. And that is a fraction of what is being doled out now. Everybody gets the same -- the left tackle protecting the quarterback gets $5,000/month. The quarterback gets $5,000/month. It breeds acrimony and self-centeredness. And then the whole free agency every year -- it's a bidding contest. It's unfettered free agency right now. That's got to change."

title: Nick Saban on sputtering Protect College Sports Act: "I think a lot of the issues that we have right now could be resolved in this bill, if people would get on board with it. But it's not perfect. But the thing about it is, democracy is not perfect, but it's better than everything else. Tell me something better. This bill is not perfect, but it's better than everything else, and it's certainly 100 times better than what we have now, and it probably solves 80% of the problems. We want to stay focused on 20% of the problems that it doesn't solve. But if you just solve one transfer, control NIL to some degree in terms of a level playing field and five years of eligibility, you would answer your own question about the guy from the Cleveland Browns. Five years of eligibility." To be clear: Dae'quan Wright (who is 22 years old) is returning from the NFL to college for his 5th year of eligibility. In fact, attorneys litigating some of the current eligibility cases have cited the PCSA as allowing eligibility for Class of 2022 players like Wright. https://t.co/nP5wtXlpbN

title: Sources: Texans defensive end Dylan Horton tore Achilles By Aaron Wilson Texans veteran defensive end Dylan Horton suffered a serious injury Monday morning, a torn Achilles tendon, according to four league sources. "He's going through it," a source said. "Tore his Achilles." This is a tough development for Horton and a Texans defense already dealing with injuries. Horton was likely going to be the Texans' fourth defensive end on the depth chart behind All-Pro edges Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter and three-time Pro Bowl selection Jadeveon Clowney. Horton, a lymphoma survivor who previously won the Ed Block Courage award in balloting from his teammates, got hurt during the latter portion of practice during team drills. He was helped off the field by trainers. Horton, a 6-foot-4, 275-pound former fourth-round draft pick from TCU, has appeared in 39 career games and has recorded 55 tackles, three tackles for losses, a half-sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He was on several of the Texans' special teams units. Clowney is sidelined with a lower leg injury. It's regarded as a short-term injury "We expected Clowney to be back," Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. "He's dealing with a lower leg injury. He'll be back soon." Defensive end Domonique Robinson is out this week with a calf injury, and defensive end-tackle Logan Hall has missed the past few practices. Solomon Byrd and Robinson are the leading candidates for the fourth defensive end role, unless Hall slides outside. The Texans previously made trade inquiries regarding Horton, Robinson and Byrd with the San Francisco 49ers, per a league source. More movement could unfold at the position heading into the roster cutdown to 53 players Sunday. Several players didn't practice Monday, including wide receiver Tank Dell, who hasn't suffered a setback and is working out independently in return from major knee injury, rookie linebacker Wade Woodaz, who underwent successful surgery to repair a broken thumb Monday and is expected to practice with a cast on in roughly a week, running backs Jawhar Jordan (strained hip flexor) and Noah Whittington (ankle), cornerback Collin Wright (soft-tissue injury), linebacker Jake Hansen (ankle) and tight end Brevin Jordan (knee). Running back British Brooks returned to practice from a broken hand that required surgery to repair the damage. Having wide receiver Jaylin Noel participate fully provides a boost to the passing game, in addition to trading for New England Patriots wide receiver Kayshon Boutte. Noel has recovered from a strained hamstring and a broken right pinkie finger. "Jaylin’s done a good job of bouncing back, getting back into the swing of things, just continuing to get reps to build up his stamina to get out there," Ryans said. "He's done a great job of progressing on the side, and he's looked fine as he's been out there with the team during the team reps." NOTES: The Texans waived-injured linebacker Marte Mapu, waived wide receiver Jha'Quan Jackson and released Juwan Winfree with the signings of running back Deuce Vaughn, linebacker Caleb Johnson and former All-Pro special-teams ace and safety George Odom. ... Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw touchdown passes to wide receivers Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson. The pass to Hutchinson was a deep strike behind All-Pro corner Derek Stingley Jr. up the sideline. ... Stroud was intercepted by Pro Bowl middle linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair. ... Ryans said that the practice wasn't up to the standard and that the team needs to improve as the top-ranked defense flexed its collective muscle against an offense that's still a work in progress. "Today wasn't good enough from the standpoint of how we move the football," Ryans said. "It wasn't good enough. I challenged our guys to make sure we pick it up and operate that way. We have a lot to improve upon. We're not there yet. We still have a lot of work to do." ... The Texans travel Tuesday for a Wednesday morning joint practice at the Carolina Panthers' training facility prior to wrapping up the preseason Friday night at Bank of America Stadium. “I think a lot of people try to put a quantitative measure on how joint practices are equivalent to a game," Ryans said. "I don't think anybody really knows that, but I feel like you get really good reps with your ones in joint practices. You can manufacture certain situations that you may not get if we just lined it up and played in a game. That's the purpose of joint practice. I think it breaks the monotony, you go against a different scheme and you get good work versus different schemes. That's the purpose of it. I think ones get a lot of value out of doing those reps. When you have like-minded people who can come together and get good work in, joint practices are beneficial." ... Tight end Foster Moreau caught a touchdown pass from backup quarterback Davis Mills. .. Three-time NFL Defensive Player J.J. Watt, a retired Texans defensive end now working for CBS as an analyst with Jim Nantz, attended practice. “I'm very fond of J.J. Watt," Ryans said. "Everything he stands for, the type of player that he is, the man that he is, everything he's doing post-career. He's just a guy I always keep an eye on, always just proud of the work that he's done for himself. I remember the young rookie coming in, living across the street from me. My old neighbor, just to see him grow now into a husband, family man, a businessman, I’m just proud of everything he stands for and everything that's ahead for him. He has the Hall of Fame waiting on him, he has a gold jacket waiting on him. Whenever you can have a guy like that come out to your practice and coach up our defensive line to help him out, that's always a good thing.”

It was not quiet. -Colbie Young with a drop that popped up into a Josh Newton INT -In a one-minute drill at the end, offense struggled to get close, but no matter as Evan McPherson buried a 61-yarder to close it out 📸 Bryan Cook (6) was back in pads today. summary:
Really interesting practice for the #Bengals today. Plenty of action.

-Tacario Davis got the bump up to first team CB opposite DJ Turner (Dax Hill still rehabbing on side). Played well against Tee Higgins. Multiple PBUs and sticky in coverage. Trending up.

-Dohnte Meyers show rolls on. Hauled in a smooth back-shoulder ball from Burrow for a third-down conversion. Also, a 12-yard TD pass on third-and-goal from Flacco over the middle. 

-Kyle Dugger with a great play for PBU on Mike Gesicki on fourth-and-2. 

-Hell of a day for the Ja'Marr vs DJ Turner battle. It was not quiet. 

-Colbie Young with a drop that popped up into a Josh Newton INT

-In a one-minute drill at the end, offense struggled to get close, but no matter as Evan McPherson buried a 61-yarder to close it out

📸 Bryan Cook (6) was back in pads today. Not participating in team drills, but much closer to returning.

-Dohnte Meyers show rolls on. Hauled in a smooth back-shoulder ball from Burrow for a third-down conversion. Also, a 12-yard TD pass on third-and-goal from Flacco over the middle. 

-Kyle Dugger with a great play for PBU on Mike Gesicki on fourth-and-2. 

-Hell of a day for the Ja'Marr vs DJ Turner battle. It was not quiet. 

-Colbie Young with a drop that popped up into a Josh Newton INT

-In a one-minute drill at the end, offense struggled to get close, but no matter as Evan McPherson buried a 61-yarder to close it out

full_text:
A few injury updates from Mike LaFleur today: 

- RB Jeremiyah Love's high ankle sprain is "doing well, progressing well" and Love is in the next phase of his recovery, LaFleur said. However, Love will not practice or play this week, LaFleur added. 

- QB Carson Beck's status for Friday night's preseason finale against the Packers is "TBD", LaFleur said. But Beck had a "good" throwing session last week.

- LaFleur called S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson's injury "a little bit of a rib issue."

- P Blake Gillikin is "good" but won't punt this week. LaFleur isn't worry about anything long-term but said there's no point him punting this week.

- Before the team announced that RB Trey Benson was waived/injured" on Monday, LaFleur said the Cardinals were taking it "one day at a time" and would have a better understanding of Benson's status after Friday's game.

title: Day 19 notes: - Shortest padded practice of camp. It was essentially a walkthrough. - Trey Pipkins was first up at left guard, rotating with Kayode Awosika, who Mike McDaniel said has all but secured the job. - Branson Taylor remains out of practice. He hasn’t practiced since last Tuesday, missing the last three practices. - DJ Uiagalelei threw two interceptions, one to Donte Jackson and another to Myles Purchase. - The 1-on-1s were pretty back-and-forth today. Teair Tart was vocal, yelling “great ass whooping” after Nick Barrett beat Jake Slaughter w a bull rush. Slaughter later got a win over Dalvin Tomlinson. Tart was yelling and encouraging the defensive line throughout the period. - Keaton Mitchell has missed two straight practices, McDaniel said he had a “setback.” Kyle Kennard, Branson Taylor and Eric Rogers have missed the last three practices.
summary:
Day 19 notes:

- Shortest padded practice of camp. It was essentially a walkthrough.

- Trey Pipkins was first up at left guard, rotating with Kayode Awosika, who Mike McDaniel said has all but secured the job.

- Branson Taylor remains out of practice. He hasn’t practiced since last Tuesday, missing the last three practices.

- DJ Uiagalelei threw two interceptions, one to Donte Jackson and another to Myles Purchase.

- The 1-on-1s were pretty back-and-forth today. Teair Tart was vocal, yelling “great ass whooping” after Nick Barrett beat Jake Slaughter w a bull rush. Slaughter later got a win over Dalvin Tomlinson. Tart was yelling and encouraging the defensive line throughout the period.

- Keaton Mitchell has missed two straight practices, McDaniel said he had a “setback.” Kyle Kennard, Branson Taylor and Eric Rogers have missed the last three practices.
full_text:
Day 19 notes:

- Shortest padded practice of camp. It was essentially a walkthrough.

- Trey Pipkins was first up at left guard, rotating with Kayode Awosika, who Mike McDaniel said has all but secured the job.

- Branson Taylor remains out of practice. He hasn’t practiced since last Tuesday, missing the last three practices.

- DJ Uiagalelei threw two interceptions, one to Donte Jackson and another to Myles Purchase.

- The 1-on-1s were pretty back-and-forth today. Teair Tart was vocal, yelling “great ass whooping” after Nick Barrett beat Jake Slaughter w a bull rush. Slaughter later got a win over Dalvin Tomlinson. Tart was yelling and encouraging the defensive line throughout the period.

- Keaton Mitchell has missed two straight practices, McDaniel said he had a “setback.” Kyle Kennard, Branson Taylor and Eric Rogers have missed the last three practices.

title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer on Joe Milton: “I first remember hearing about Joe Milton when he was at the University of Michigan and everyone applauded him for how hard and how far he could throw the ball. Cool. That’s awesome. Go be in a carnival somewhere. That’s not what playing an NFL quarterback is. It’s not. … You’re throwing through small windows, you’re throwing over people, you’re changing arm slots. “So to me, arm strength is cool. Go to the fair and win a teddy bear. But you got to play quarterback. And that’s what I think you see Joe learning is he’s playing quarterback. And he’s playing quarterback at a high level. He’s checking the ball down. He’s making blitz adjustments. He’s solving problems. He’s reading from his first, second to third, and even fourth progression at times. It takes time. You don’t stop learning as a quarterback. The only way to do it is to play. I’m really, really proud of him.”

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 15: Hurts and the offense didn’t have a great day in their first practice since the joint sessions against the Patriots Hurts had few mistakes that were uncharacteristic First he missed a deep pass to Hollywood Brown that would have been a touchdown if complete. Brown had his player beat but the pass was about 3 yards overthrown. Hurts also had a pass batted down in 7v7 but it is very rare. The pass came after a play where he ran the ball in 7v7 because he held it too long and didn’t attempt a pass. Part of the reason for the struggles was the defensive line had a big day getting in the backfield quite a bit. Hurts not turning the ball over despite the pressure was a positive. The best throw of the day for Hurts was a pass down the right sideline to Hollywood Brown for about a 35ish yard gain. But even that pass felt like with a better throw it could have been a longer gain. Hurts had a few completions over the middle but nothing really beyond 10ish yards Not the best day for the passing offense Day 15 Stats: 13/21, 0 TD, 0 INT 2026 Stats: 179/262, 14 TD, 0 INT
